Situation1: There is a scheduled family gathering on the calendar.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Story: I woke up to the shrill ring of my phone in the middle of the night. My friend’s voice trembled on the other end, words tumbling out between sobs about a sudden, devastating loss in their family. I sat up, heart pounding, listening as they poured out their pain, desperate for comfort. I wanted to be there for them, to offer the support and understanding they needed right now. But as I glanced at the calendar on my nightstand, I was reminded of the family gathering scheduled for tomorrow—a day my grandchildren had been looking forward to all week. They expected me to be present, to laugh and play and make memories together. The weight of both roles pressed down on me. My friend needed me in this dark hour, but my family was counting on me too. I felt torn, caught between the urge to be a supportive friend and the responsibility of being a loving grandfather. The expectations from both sides swirled in my mind, leaving me restless and uncertain as I sat in the quiet darkness, phone still pressed to my ear.
